description: Fix data isolation for dashboard, alerts (display side), and report generation. These are independent of FEAT-002's per-resource guards but depend on SecurityAlert.createdBy existing (FEAT-001). Dashboard currently issues global queries with no user filter — analysts see everyone's stats. Reports buildReportData has no user filter. This feature also updates the verify route to use baselineSha256 (from FEAT-001) and adds hash input validation.
steps: 1. Modify server/src/controllers/dashboardController.js — getStats(): wrap all queries in user-scoped filters. For admin (req.user.role==='admin'): queries stay global (current behavior). For analyst: all MonitoredFile queries get filter {createdBy:req.user._id}. All MonitoredFolder queries get filter {createdBy:req.user._id}. SecurityAlert queries get filter {createdBy:req.user._id}. DigitalSignature queries get filter {createdBy:req.user._id}. IntegrityEvent queries: filter by folderId in the user's folders (query user's folderIds first, then use {folderId:{$in:userFolderIds}}). recentAuditLogs: for admin only — analysts receive empty array. alertSeverityBreakdown aggregation: add $match for createdBy filter. eventsOverTime aggregation: add folderId $in filter for analysts.

2. Modify server/src/services/reportService.js — buildReportData(): accept a second parameter userId and userRole. When userRole!=='admin', add {createdBy:userId} to MonitoredFile.find() and SecurityAlert.find(), and filter IntegrityEvent by folderId $in (user's folder IDs). Update generateCSVReport to use baselineSha256 and currentSha256 columns (field names changed in FEAT-001).
3. Modify server/src/controllers/reportController.js — generateReport(): pass req.user._id and req.user.role to buildReportData().

4. Modify server/src/routes/verify.js — POST /verify/hash: add express-validator rule: body('expectedHash').matches(/^[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$/).withMessage('expectedHash must be a 64-character hex string'). Import validate middleware and apply. Also normalize expectedHash.toLowerCase() before comparison (already done but make explicit). POST /verify/file/:id: add same 64-hex validation on any submitted hash in body; also ensure comparison uses file.baselineSha256 (change from file.sha256).

5. Modify server/src/controllers/fileController.js — verifyUploadedFile(): add express-validator rule in the route for expectedHash: body('expectedHash').matches(/^[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$/) — add this validation to the route in server/src/routes/files.js for POST /verify. Also use crypto.timingSafeEqual explicitly in compareHashes (already done in hashService.js compareHashes — verify it is used in verifyUploadedFile; if compareHashes is called, it is fine).

6. Modify server/src/routes/files.js: add express-validator body validation for POST /verify: body('expectedHash').matches(/^[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$/).withMessage('expectedHash must be a valid 64-character SHA-256 hex string'). Import body and validate.
7. Verify that recentAlerts in dashboardController are filtered by createdBy for analysts so no other user's alert data (including filePaths and hashes) leaks into the response.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/dashboard/stats for analyst returns only counts/events/alerts for that user's resources.
Analyst dashboard never exposes other users' file names, paths, or hashes.
Admin dashboard returns global stats (unchanged behavior).
POST /api/verify/hash with expectedHash not matching /^[a-fA-F0-9]{64}$/ returns 400.
buildReportData scopes file and alert queries to the requesting user for analysts.
